## Why This Is Asked

Tests real-world CAPA expertise in an edge/CDN environment where cross-region effects and tenant isolation are critical. Evaluates ability to design concrete models, metrics, and rollout controls for distributed systems.

## Key Concepts

- CAPA data model: evidence artifacts, lineage mapping, ownership tracking, timestamps
- Region-aware lifecycle: detect, contain, remediate, verify with SLAs per region
- API design: idempotent create/update with logs, traces, and policy linkage
- Metrics: containment time, leakage rate, recurrence, MTTR
- RCA template: root cause analysis, corrective actions, preventive actions, verification
- Canary strategy: phased rollouts with automated rollback and monitoring

## Success Criteria

- Demonstrates understanding of distributed system incident response
- Shows practical API design with observability integration
- Provides measurable metrics and clear SLAs
- Addresses tenant isolation and edge-specific challenges

## Correct Answer
Use template.metadata.name: my-app-{{cluster}} so each generated Application gets a unique name based on the cluster value.

## Why Other Options Are Wrong
- Option B would create name collisions across clusters, since the same fixed name would be used for all generated Apps.
- Option C misuses the destination field; cluster differentiation for the Application name should come from the template name, not the destination.
- Option D defeats the purpose of a single ApplicationSet generating many apps and adds unnecessary maintenance.

## Key Concepts
- ApplicationSet templating
- Generators (cluster) and template.name placeholders
- Unique naming for generated Applications

## Real-World Application
- When deploying to many clusters, using cluster-derived names helps administrators quickly identify which App belongs to which cluster and simplifies drift and health monitoring.
